question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x$ is

$$
\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}.
$$

Substituting the above definition into the equation $8\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8(\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}}) & =1 \\ 8({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & ={e}^{x}+{e}^{-x} \\ 8{e}^{x}-8{e}^{-x} & ={e}^{x}+{e}^{-x} \\ 7{e}^{x} & =9{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we multiply both sides of the equation by ${e}^{x}$ and solve the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}\cdot 7{e}^{x} & ={e}^{x}\cdot 9{e}^{-x} \\ {e}^{2x} & =\frac{9}{7} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{9}{7}) \\ 2x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{9}{7}) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{9}{7})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only real solution is

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{9}{7}).
$$
